gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-granth: Letters here are pressed flat like pen-nib bowls, and the eye glides through without catching on a closed-up counter. Noto Sans Grantha, a sans-serif, holds that smooth footing under Stencilia's striking display shapes.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-gunjal: Stencilia draws structural, striking letters with a compact gap between x-height and ascender line. Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi is the better one for steady reading, with crayon-thick lowercase strokes and terminals cut back to leave generous gaps.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-jp: Stencilia brings structural, striking display letters, with open gaps where its curves end and a compact band between x-height and ascender line. Noto Sans JP simply sweeps open and reads quickly.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-kharos: Stencilia carries the structural, striking display work, with open gaps at curve terminals and a compact span from x-height to ascender line. And Noto Sans Kharoshthi lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase, so you can size it to taste.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Chiseled and bold, Stencilia sets structural display letters beside a sans whose generous openings look like notches cut in wood. Small letters stand proud there, almost capital-sized, and go down easily.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-lao: Lowercase pushed well above the usual height makes this body font read easily, with mouths that stay open on c, e, and a. Noto Sans Lao handles the running text, while Stencilia delivers structural, striking display letters.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Noto Sans Lepcha is a sans-serif whose lowercase carries the stature of cast iron capitals, with curves keeping a wide opening. Paragraphs of it feel approachable and unhurried.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Noto Sans Limbu has small letters with real height and curves that look like they are gaping. Noto Sans Limbu keeps long stretches of text approachable and unfussy, while Stencilia makes the structural statement above.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-mahaja: Lowercase stands up against the capitals here, and the e has a wide throat like a funnel. Noto Sans Mahajani does the everyday reading, while Stencilia does the striking, structural display work.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-noto-sans-marche: Stencilia gives structural, striking display letters, with open curve terminals and a compact gap between x-height and ascender line. Noto Sans Marchen then adds proud, near-capital small letters whose curves end in clear daylight.
